(p-202) Sūrat Quraysh

Makkī, and its verses are four.

﴿For the covenant (ilāf) of the Quraysh﴾ is connected to His words, exalted is He: ﴿so let them worship﴾, and the fāʾ (so) is because of the meaning of a condition in the speech; for the meaning is: the blessings of God, exalted is He, upon them are not to be counted, so if they do not worship Him for all His other blessings, then let them worship Him for this great blessing. It has also been said that it is connected to a suppressed element whose estimate is: We did what We did of destroying the People of the Elephant for the covenant of... etc. It has also been said that its estimate is: Marvel at the covenant of... etc. It has also been said that it is connected to what precedes it, namely His words, exalted is He: ﴿and He made them like eaten husks﴾; and this is supported by the fact that in the codex of Ubayy they are one single sūrah, so there is no separation. The meaning is: He destroyed those from Abyssinia who intended them, so that people would hear of it and stand in greater awe of them, and they would be shown exceeding respect, until security is established for them in their two journeys, so that no one dares to attack them. The Quraysh had two journeys: they would travel in winter to Yemen and in summer to Syria, where they would trade and engage in commerce; and in their two journeys they were secure, because they were the people of the sacred precinct of God and the custodians of His mighty House, so no one would be molested while people were snatching and being plundered all around. The word ilāf is from your saying: "ālaftu al-makān īlāfan," when you became familiar with the place. It was also read "li-ilāf Quraysh," meaning: for their familiarity (muwālafah). It has been said: one says "aliftuhu ilfan wa ilāfan" (I became accustomed to it). It was also read "li-ilf Quraysh." And "Quraysh" is the offspring of al-Naḍr ibn Kinānah; they were named by the diminutive of "qirsh" (qirsh), which is a huge creature in the sea that attacks ships and cannot be subdued except with fire; the diminutive is for magnification. It has also been said that it is from "qarsh," which means earning, because they were earners through their trade and their travel in the lands.

Abu al-Su'ud's commentary (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on Surah 106, verse 2:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿for the familiarity of the Quraysh, their familiarity with the caravan of winter and summer﴾ is a substitute (badal) for the first (phrase). "Rihlata" (the journey) is the object of "ilafihim" (their familiarity). Its being singular, although what is meant is the two journeys of winter and summer, is to avoid confusion (li-amn al-iltibas). The omission of the object of "ilaf" at first, and the substitution of this phrase for it, serve to magnify its matter and to remind of the great blessing in it. It has been read as "li-ya'lafa Quraysha ilfuhum rihlata al-shita' wa al-sayf" (so that the Quraysh may become accustomed, their accustomedness to the journey of winter and summer). It has also been read as "ruhlata" with a dhamma, and that is the direction to which one travels.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 106, verses 3–4:

﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House﴾ ﴿who fed them﴾ by means of those two journeys, in which they were established through their being neighbours of it. (p-203) ﴿from hunger﴾ severe, which they had been in before those two journeys. It is also said: what is meant by it is the famine in which they ate carrion and bones. ﴿And He made them secure from fear﴾ great, its extent cannot be measured, and it is the fear of the People of the Elephant, or the fear of being snatched away in their land and on their travels. It is also said: it is the fear of leprosy, so that it does not afflict them in their land.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surat Quraysh, Allah the Exalted will grant him ten good deeds for each of those who circumambulated the Ka'ba and performed i'tikaf in it."
